request:
I run a susu group at the market in Kumasi and I want to stop keeping the records in an exercise book. I need to start a group and add the members, each with their name and phone number. Every round, members pay in their contribution, and I record who paid, for which round, and how much in cedis. At the end of a round one member collects the pot, and the pot is everything that was paid in for that round, nothing more and nothing less. Each round has only one collector, and a member can collect only once, so if someone has already collected, they cannot collect again. Once a round has been collected, nobody can pay more into that round, and a round where nobody has paid anything cannot be collected. Contributions must be more than zero. For any member I want a statement showing how much they have paid in altogether and how much they have received. I also want to see the list of members and the collections made so far.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Does every member pay the same fixed amount each round, or can amounts differ from member to member, and can one member pay more than once in the same round?
A: No, record whatever each member actually paid; the pot is the total paid in for that round.
Q: Do you choose who collects each round freely, or is there a set order of collectors decided at the start?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Must rounds go strictly one after another, so nobody can pay into round 3 until round 2 has been collected?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built the system in `app.py`, and all 8 automated tests pass. Your records are saved in a file called `susu.db` in the same folder. It only keeps records and does not move or hold any real money.

**What you can do:**
- **POST `/groups`**: start a group by giving it a name.
- **POST `/groups/{groupId}/members`**: add a member with a name and phone number. Both are required.
- **GET `/groups/{groupId}/members`**: see the list of members with their names and phone numbers.
- **POST `/groups/{groupId}/payments`**: record that a member paid an amount in cedis for a round. A member can pay any amount, and can pay more than once in the same round.
- **POST `/groups/{groupId}/collections`**: record which member collected the pot for a round. The system adds up everything paid in for that round and saves that as the pot.
- **GET `/groups/{groupId}/collections`**: see the collections made so far: which round, who collected and how much the pot was.
- **GET `/groups/{groupId}/members/{memberId}/statement`**: see how much one member has paid in altogether and how much they have received.

**What the system refuses:**
- A member with no name or no phone number.
- A payment of zero or less.
- A payment or collection for someone who isn't a member of that group.
- Any more payments into a round that has already been collected.
- A second collector for the same round.
- A member collecting a second time.
- Collecting a round where nobody has paid anything.
- Typing in the pot amount yourself.

**Choices I made where you had no preference:**
- You choose who collects each round; there is no fixed order set at the start.
- Rounds don't have to go in order, so you can record money for any round that hasn't been collected yet.
- Round numbers start at 1.
- Amounts can include pesewas, up to 2 decimal places (for example 20.25). Money is stored in whole pesewas so the totals always add up exactly.

**Still waiting on your answer:** phone numbers show in the member list to anyone who can open it. Tell me if you'd like to limit who can see them. I haven't added any protection because you didn't ask for it.

plan.summary: This plan replaces your exercise book with a simple record-keeping system for your susu group. You can start a group, add members (name and phone number), record each payment a member makes for a round in cedis, and record who collects the pot at the end of a round. The system works out the pot for you: it is exactly the total paid in for that round. You can see the list of members, the list of collections so far, and a statement for any member showing how much they have paid in and how much they have received. Each member can pay any amount above zero, and may pay more than once in the same round; every payment is kept. Where you had no preference, we chose the simplest option. You pick the collector for each round when you record the collection; there is no fixed order set at the start. Rounds do not have to go strictly one after another, so money can be recorded for any round that has not yet been collected. This system only keeps records. It does not move or hold any real money. Question for you: members' phone numbers will appear in the member list. Should anyone who can see the list be able to see them, or would you like to limit who sees them? We have not added any protection for this because you did not ask for it.

data.name: Payment
fields: which round it is for (round number)

data.name: Collection
fields: pot amount in cedis (worked out by the system as the total paid in for that round)

endpoints.does: Starts a new susu group with the name you give it.
Adds a member to the group with their name and phone number.
Shows the list of all members in the group.
Records that a member paid an amount in cedis for a given round.
Records that a chosen member collected the pot for a given round. The system adds up everything paid in for that round and saves that total as the pot.
Shows all the collections made so far: which round, who collected, and how much the pot was.
Shows one member's statement: the total they have paid in altogether and the total they have received from collections.

rules: A member must have a name and a phone number; refuse to add a member without both.
A payment must be more than zero cedis; refuse zero or negative amounts.
A payment or collection must be for a member who belongs to that group; refuse it otherwise.
Refuse any payment into a round that has already been collected.
Each round can have only one collector; refuse a second collection for the same round.
A member can collect only once; refuse a collection for a member who has already collected.
Refuse to record a collection for a round where nobody has paid anything.
The pot is always exactly the total paid in for that round; it cannot be typed in or changed by hand.
